# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

## Problem
`implement.py finish` runs the test suite via `skill/test_cache.run_cached` with a direct `pytest` command, so it does NOT set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1`. The canonical `run_tests.py` DOES set this marker (see `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` around the live-repo mutation guard) to stand down the inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` pytest plugin.

Without the marker, the inner pytest arms the guard. Tests that `monkeypatch.setattr(audit_runner.subprocess, 'Popen', lambda ...)` (e.g. `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py`) leave the patch active when the guard's `pytest_runtest_teardown` hook runs (guard teardown executes before monkeypatch fixture undo). The guard then calls `subprocess.run`, which hits the `_MockProcess` return value and raises:
`TypeError: 'skill.audit.tests.test_audit_queue_integration._MockProcess' object does not support the context manager protocol`.
This cascades into every subsequent test error plus a `pytest_sessionfinish` failure, blocking `implement.py finish` (AC5 status).

## Evidence
Reproduced during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1: `implement.py finish` full gate failed; running the same pytest command with `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` passes and the finish completes.

## Expected
`implement.py run_tests` should set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` in the subprocess environment when invoking the inner pytest (mirroring `run_tests.py`), so the outer/inner guard ownership is consistent and finish does not crash on subprocess-patching tests. Alternatively, route `implement.py`'s test execution through the canonical test-skill runner.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `implement.py finish` full-suite gate passes on `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` without an externally-set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the marker is set for the inner pytest invocation (or that the guard stands down).
- [ ] No double-guard reporting; the outer guard still detects real repo mutation.

Discovered during SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1.
data.title: implement.py run_tests bypasses LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE, so finish hits live-repo-guard crash on subprocess-patching tests

## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo.** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo — see Open Question 1.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence: `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, and launcher/hook inspection.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — see Open Question 1): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV** – cwd-independent wl invocation and real diagnostics (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? Options: (A) non-destructive evidence only (`/proc/<pid>/environ`, launcher/hook inspection, git trace2); (B) also spawn a live agent session and dump its env; (C) both. **Recommended:** C — trace2 + launcher inspection first, then one controlled fresh-session env dump to prove the end-to-end state. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q3 (regression-check placement):** The AC "a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables" — where should the check live? Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
data.title: Investigate external launcher that exported GIT_DIR into agent/test sessions

# Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`

## Problem statement

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` refuses
to `wl close --force <parent>` whenever *any* descendant is not itself in the
close-candidate set (candidates come only from `getCandidateItems()`, which
returns `stage: in_review` items). Descendants that are already terminal
(`stage: done` / `status: deleted`) therefore look like "collateral" and
falsely block the parent's close, even though a terminal child needs no
action. This was observed during the ContextHub v1.0.16 release, where the
auto-close step closed **0 of 14** released `in_review` items.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer/operator.** As the producer running a
  release, I want the post-release close step to close a released parent whose
  only non-candidate descendants are already terminal, so I do not have to
  force-close it by hand or leave released work in `in_review`.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline.** As `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, I
  want a correct, non-sweeping scope signal: terminal descendants are
  harmless, genuinely non-terminal descendants must still block, and a
  descendant held back for producer review should be reported as such.
- **Secondary user — audit/release operators.** As an operator reading the
  release log, I want the refusal reason to name the *real* cause (e.g.
  `needsProducerReview`), not a generic collateral list, so I know what to do
  next.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The collateral-exclusion set excludes descendants that are already terminal
   (`stage: done` or `status: deleted`), so a parent whose only non-candidate
   descendants are terminal is closed. *(Core defect — already implemented by
   sibling `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`, commit `9c9d55b9`; keep and verify.)*
2. A descendant skipped solely because `needsProducerReview=true` is reported
   with a **distinct** refusal reason (not lumped under the generic
   "collateral" list), while the parent is still refused. *(Remaining work.)*
3. Genuine non-terminal descendants (`open`/`blocked`/`in_progress`/
   `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`) still block the parent close — the scope
   guard must not be weakened. *(Already implemented; keep and verify.)*
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/
   `getItemLifecycleFn` cover: (a) all-done descendants → parent closes;
   (b) one non-terminal descendant → parent refused; (c) an npr=true
   descendant → parent refused with a distinct reason. (a) and (b) exist;
   (c) is missing. *(Remaining work.)*
5. `npm run build` and all existing suites pass.
6. All related documentation (release-process docs and ship/audit skill
   references) reflects the distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting.

## Constraints

- Minimal, additive change to `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`; do not weaken the
  out-of-scope scope guard (`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H AC9/AC10`).
- Do not change the existing child producer-review override/absorption logic
  (`SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q`).
- Unit tests must inject fakes and must never mutate the live worklog
  (`SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS`).
- Follow build → test → commit order; never commit with a failing suite.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` already filters terminal descendants out of the
  collateral set (~lines 541-559), added by **`SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`**
  ("Ship close terminal-descendant exclusion", commit `9c9d55b9`, on `dev`) as
  defence-in-depth for `SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP` (cascade descendants of an
  audit-approved parent). AC1 and AC3 are therefore already satisfied.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` already covers
  (a) all-terminal descendants → close, (b) non-terminal descendant → refuse,
  and a mixed terminal/non-terminal case; all 23 tests pass. AC4(c) is absent.
- AC2 (distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting) is **not**
  implemented: the refusal reason at ~line 561 is
  `Refused: --force close would sweep descendant(s) outside the candidate set: …`
  regardless of cause.
- The cascade policy (`SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP`, completed) makes fully-terminal
  subtrees common, further reducing the original false-refusal occurrence.
- Related but distinct: `SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5` (ship release must *verify*
  in-scope items were actually closed — open).

## Desired change

1. In `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, classify a non-candidate, non-terminal
   descendant that is held back solely because `needsProducerReview=true`
   separately from generic collateral, and surface a distinct refusal reason
   (the parent is still refused).
2. Add the AC4(c) regression test asserting the distinct reason.
3. Update the relevant release/ship documentation for the new reporting.
4. Re-verify AC1/AC3 by running the existing terminal-descendant tests and
   `npm run build`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` collateral
  classification and refusal-reason construction (~lines 530-575); add the
  distinct npr classification.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — add the AC4(c)
  npr=true descendant test.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` (and/or the ship/audit skill reference docs) —
  document the distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the core false-refusal (AC1/AC3) is already fixed on `dev`
  by `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` (commit `9c9d55b9`) and its tests pass, so the
  residual scope is AC2 + AC4(c) + verification. *If the producer disagrees,
  re-scope or close the item (see Appendix OPEN QUESTION).*
- **Risk — scope guard regression (medium):** touching the collateral
  classification could accidentally let genuinely non-terminal descendants be
  swept by `wl close --force`. **Mitigation:** keep AC3 covered by the existing
  non-terminal refusal tests and add the AC4(c) case without relaxing AC3.
- **Risk — over-broad npr reporting (low):** classifying *all*
  `needsProducerReview` descendants as a distinct reason could mislabel ones
  that are candidates/terminal. **Mitigation:** classify only non-candidate,
  non-terminal descendants held back solely by `needsProducerReview`.
- **Risk — documentation drift (low):** release docs may already describe the
  terminal exclusion but not the distinct npr reason. **Mitigation:** AC6
  explicitly updates the docs.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the broader out-of-scope/parent-coverage themes
  (`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`) and the `inherited_pass` tracking-hygiene issue
  (`SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`) are **out of scope** here and remain tracked by
  their own items.

## Related work

- **`SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`** (completed) — terminal-descendant exclusion;
  already implemented AC1/AC3 of this item.
- **`SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP`** (completed) — cascade children of an
  audit-approved parent to `completed`/`done` (the producer's stated policy
  and the root-cause counterpart).
- **`SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q`** (completed) — override/absorb
  `needsProducerReview` on children of a release-ready parent.
- **`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`** (completed) — parent-coverage / out-of-scope rules
  for child audits (the scope guard being preserved).
- **`SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`** — audit runner `inherited_pass` bypasses the
  children-stage block (related tracking-hygiene concern).
- **`SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5`** (open) — ship release must verify in-scope items
  are actually closed before reporting success.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The core false-refusal (AC1/AC3) is already implemented by
  `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` and all existing tests pass. Should this item remain
  open for the residual `needsProducerReview` distinct-reporting scope
  (AC2/AC4c), or be closed as substantially resolved?"
  — **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking assumption applied).**
  **Recommended:** keep this item open and narrow the remaining work to AC2
  (distinct npr refusal reason) + AC4(c) (regression test) + verification.
  Rationale: the item's author explicitly listed AC2/AC4(c) as desired
  behaviour, and the sibling work item records this item as "the primary/
  broader ship-side item". Answer: *assumed keep-open/narrow* by Map; producer
  may re-scope or close. Source: work-item descriptions of
  `SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP` and `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`; code inspection of
  `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` and
  `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs`.

- Q: "Is the `needsProducerReview` descendant actually reachable as a
  collateral refusal?"
  — Answer: yes (research finding). A descendant with
  `needsProducerReview=true` in `stage: in_review` is a candidate; if it is
  **not** covered by an audit-ready ancestor it is skipped rather than closed,
  so it is absent from `toClose`/`candidateIds` and lands in the generic
  collateral set. Source: code inspection of
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`).

- Q: "Could the terminal-descendant fix have removed the need for this item
  entirely?"
  — Answer: no. `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` addressed only the terminal-descendant
  false positive (AC1/AC3); AC2 distinct reporting and AC4(c) remain, as does
  the high-priority release-blocking symptom. Source: `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`
  AC1-AC3 and its description of this item as the primary/broader item.

- **SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT** – Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout (completed)

## Problem Statement

`detect_regressions()` in `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (line 753) defines a regression as *any* transition away from `completed`/`in_review`:

```python
is_regressed = not (cur_status == "completed" and cur_stage == "in_review")
```

This conflates a **backward slip** (e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/plan_complete`) with the **forward release transition** `completed/in_review` → `completed/done`. The ship skill closes shipped items to `stage: done`; `docs/dev/release-process.md` treats `completed/done` as a terminal (released) state, compatible with `completed/in_review`.

## Observed Impact

Standup window 2026-09-28 06:00 → 2026-09-29 06:00 (SorraAgents). The report's Regressions section listed **80 items**. All 80 were `completed/in_review` in the pre-window snapshot and are now `completed/done` — i.e. all 80 were *released* (release merge `release/dev-to-main-20260928210652`), not regressed. Zero items actually slipped backwards, so the section was 100% false positives and useless.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `detect_regressions()` only flags a genuine backward slip: an item that was `completed`/`in_review` before the window and is now in a non-terminal state (status != `completed`, or stage in `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`). The transition `completed/in_review` → `completed/done` must NOT be flagged.
2. Add regression tests in `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` proving:
   - `completed/in_review` → `completed/done` inside the window is NOT flagged (released);
   - `completed/in_review` → `open/plan_complete` inside the window IS flagged;
   - `completed/in_review` → `blocked/...` inside the window IS flagged;
   - `completed/in_review` → `completed/in_review` is NOT flagged;
   - the existing in-window/out-of-window gating still holds.
3. Existing standup tests pass.

## Provenance

Discovered while investigating the Regressions section of the 2026-09-29 standup report on SorraAgents. Related to SA-0MUFNU2WM00049A9 (operator-precedence fix in the same function), but distinct: that fix gated the predicate on `in_window()`; this bug is the definition of `is_regressed` itself, which still misclassifies the forward `in_review` → `done` release transition.

# voice-input: provide clear feedback when voice input is enabled, disabled and sending

**Headline.** Give the operator an unmistakable, unit-tested acknowledgement at
each voice-input transition — recording started, recording stopped, and the
capture/submission outcome — via an `info` notification plus the existing footer
indicator (and optionally an audible cue), and explicitly report when nothing
was captured. This closes the current gap where a mis-press, a swallowed
`Ctrl+Space` or a silent capture is indistinguishable from a successful
dictation.

## Problem statement

Operators cannot reliably tell whether the `voice-input` extension is currently
listening, has stopped, or has actually sent their dictated prompt. Today the
only positive acknowledgement is a transient footer string that is easy to miss
(`🎙 Recording…`), and there is **no** notification when recording starts,
when it stops, or when the transcript is submitted — so a mis-press, a
swallowed `Ctrl+Space` or a silently empty capture all look the same as success.

## Users

- **Operator starting dictation** — "When I press `Ctrl+Space` I want an
  unmistakable acknowledgement that I am now being listened to, so I can start
  speaking immediately."
- **Operator stopping dictation** — "When I stop (or pause), I want confirmation
  that recording has stopped and that my prompt was sent."
- **Operator whose capture was empty** — "If nothing was captured I want to be
  told explicitly that nothing was sent, rather than silently losing my words."
- **Maintainer / agent** — needs deterministic, unit-testable feedback events
  rather than ad-hoc `ui.notify` calls scattered through the controller.

## Existing state

The controller (`pi-client/voice-input/controller.js`) already drives an
`idle → recording → submitting → idle` state machine and exposes `statusText()`
for a footer indicator:

| Moment | Current feedback |
|---|---|
| `start()` succeeds | footer status `🎙 Recording… (Ctrl+Space to stop)` only |
| doctor `error` on first start | `notify(..., "error")` with remedy (good) |
| doctor `warning` on first start | `notify(..., "warning")` (good) |
| `stop()` begins | footer status `⏳ Transcribing…` only |
| transcript submitted | **nothing** — editor cleared, message sent silently |
| empty transcript | `notify("… no speech detected — nothing was sent.", "warning")` (good) |
| abort/error | `notify(..., "error")` (good) |

Gaps: no explicit *start* acknowledgement, no explicit *stop* acknowledgement,
no explicit *submitted* acknowledgement, no explicit confirmation that an empty
capture was reported as feedback (the string exists but the event is not part of
the defined feedback contract), and no way to get an audible cue when the
operator is not looking at the footer.

## Desired change

Introduce one centralised, testable feedback path in the controller that emits a
distinct acknowledgement for each transition, with the **capture outcome**
reported on stop:

1. **Start recording (enabled).** `Ctrl+Space` / `/voice-input` from `idle` →
   recording starts → an `info` notification such as
   `🎙 Voice input enabled — listening… (Ctrl+Space to stop)`, plus the existing
   footer indicator.
2. **Stop recording (disabled).** A second `Ctrl+Space`/`/voice-input`, or the
   silence auto-stop → recording stops → an `info` notification such as
   `🔇 Voice input disabled — processing…`, plus the footer changing to
   `⏳ Transcribing…`.
3. **Capture outcome on stop (sending).** When the stopped capture produced a
   non-empty transcript it is submitted (existing behaviour) and acknowledged
   with an `info` notification such as
   `📤 Voice input: sending “<first words>…”` (truncated). **If nothing was
   captured**, an explicit `warning` reports `Voice input: nothing captured —
   nothing was sent.` (retaining today's behaviour and making it part of the
   defined contract).
4. **Audible cue (optional, configurable).** A short terminal bell for each
   transition, controlled by a new `feedbackSound` setting
   (`PI_VOICE_INPUT_FEEDBACK_SOUND`, default `true`), wired through an injectable
   `playSound` dependency so tests can assert it.

Wording stays concise (one line), uses the existing `"info"` level for
state/success and keeps `"warning"`/`"error"` for the empty-capture and failure
paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Start feedback:** starting a recording via `Ctrl+Space` or `/voice-input`
   (from `idle`, once the recorder has started) emits exactly one `info`
   notification that unambiguously says voice input is listening/enabled, and
   sets the footer indicator.
2. **Stop feedback:** stopping a recording — whether by a second
   `Ctrl+Space`/`/voice-input`, by the silence auto-stop, or by an abort — emits
   exactly one notification that unambiguously says recording stopped/voice input
   disabled; the footer indicator is updated/cleared.
3. **Capture-outcome feedback:** on stop, a non-empty transcript is submitted
   (`sendUserMessage` exactly once, editor cleared) and acknowledged with an
   `info` notification that says the transcript is being sent; when nothing was
   captured, an explicit `warning` notification reports that nothing was
   captured and nothing was sent, and no submission occurs.
4. **Audible feedback (configurable):** a short terminal-bell cue is emitted for
   the transitions when `feedbackSound` is enabled (settings file
   `.pi/voice-input.json` / `~/.pi/agent/voice-input.json` /
   `$PI_VOICE_INPUT_CONFIG`, or `PI_VOICE_INPUT_FEEDBACK_SOUND`, default `true`),
   and suppressed when `feedbackSound` is `false`; invalid values fall back to the
   default with a config warning.
5. **No duplication/regression, with tests:** each transition produces at most
   one feedback notification (no double-fire when manual stop races the silence
   auto-stop); existing error, doctor-warning and empty-capture notifications are
   preserved; the `submitting` state remains ignored by `toggle()`. Unit tests
   cover every transition, the `feedbackSound` on/off paths and the stop-race;
   the full project test suite passes.
6. **Documentation:** `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` (usage + settings table)
   and `docs/dev/voice-input.md` (state-machine feedback events + config table)
   are updated to describe the new feedback and the `feedbackSound` option.

## Constraints

- Follow the existing architecture: behaviour in dependency-free `.js`
  (`controller.js`, `config.js`) unit-tested with `node:test`; `index.ts` remains
  a thin `ExtensionAPI` adapter. No new runtime dependencies.
- Feedback must be non-blocking (`ctx.ui.notify` / `setStatus`), never modal, and
  must not throw — `error` events are only emitted when a listener is attached.
- Audible cue uses the terminal bell; it must be safe to emit in TUI mode and
  fully suppressible. It must never be relied on for correctness.
- The controller is a plain module: the audible cue must be injected as a
  dependency (`playSound`) so it is testable without touching `process.stdout`.
- Preserve steer/follow-up delivery semantics and the "empty transcript is never
  submitted" guarantee.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (A1 — confirmed by operator):** "enabled/disabled" refers to the
  recording lifecycle: start recording (`Ctrl+Space`) emits feedback; stop
  emits feedback.
- **Assumption (A2 — pending):** feedback is **visual by default** (notification
  + footer); the audible cue is an optional, configurable extra rather than the
  sole mechanism (terminals vary in bell support and some suppress it in panes).
- **Assumption (A3 — resolved by operator):** the capture outcome is reported on
  stop — a non-empty transcript is sent and acknowledged; if **nothing was
  captured**, that is explicitly reported. "Sending" feedback is therefore tied
  to the stop transition rather than being a standalone fourth event.
- **Risk — notification fatigue:** feedback on start, stop and outcome could be
  noisy. Mitigated by one-line wording, `info` level, exactly-once emission, and
  a config switch for the audible part; wording is trivially adjustable.
- **Risk — raw bell in TUI mode:** writing `\x07` while the TUI owns the
  terminal could interact with rendering. Mitigated by making it injectable,
  optional and default-subject-to-review; if it proves unsafe it can default to
  `false` without touching the visual ACs.
- **Scope-creep guard:** spoken/TTS feedback is **out of scope** (the repo has a
  separate `speak` skill); if wanted, raise a follow-up work item rather than
  widening this one.
- **Risk — wording churn:** tests assert the *presence and level* of the
  feedback notifications (one per transition, correct `info`/`warning`/`error`)
  rather than exact strings, so wording can be tuned without churn; the only
  string-level guarantee is that the message names the enabled/disabled/outcome
  state.
- **Failure mode:** if the terminal suppresses BEL, audible feedback silently
  no-ops; the visual notification/footer remain the source of truth in that case.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `pi-client/voice-input/controller.js` — add a single `feedback(kind, details)`
  helper; call it on start / stop / capture-outcome; accept `playSound` dep and
  `config.feedbackSound`.
- `pi-client/voice-input/config.js` — add `feedbackSound` default, env mapping
  (`PI_VOICE_INPUT_FEEDBACK_SOUND`) and boolean coercion/validation.
- `pi-client/voice-input/index.ts` — wire `playSound` (`process.stdout.write("\x07")`)
  and pass the resolved config; no behaviour change elsewhere.
- `tests/unit/test-voice-controller.mjs` — new tests: exactly-once notifications
  for start/stop/outcome, sound on/off, race between manual and silence stop,
  empty-capture path reports "nothing captured".
- `tests/unit/test-voice-config.mjs` — `feedbackSound` resolution and invalid
  value fallback.
- `pi-client/voice-input/README.md` — document the feedback behaviour and the
  `feedbackSound` setting (settings table + usage).
- `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — document the feedback events in the state-machine
  section and the config table.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUFEVYAF002GD3A** — *Voice-to-text pi extension using faster-whisper
  (Ctrl+Space)* (parent feature).
- **SA-0MUFSIB1U0088YEB** — *Extension entry point: shortcut, state machine,
  editor updates, auto-send* — the controller/state machine this builds on.
- **SA-0MUX9Y37W002T849** — *voice-input: expose transcription accuracy options …*
  — precedent for adding a config key end-to-end (config → docs → tests).
- **SA-0MUX9Y4LX000KF3P** — *voice-input: voice shortcuts that send key chords to a
  Herdr plugin pane* — precedent for controller `notify` wiring and `sendShortcut`
  injection.
- Docs: `pi-client/voice-input/README.md`, `docs/dev/voice-input.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'enabled / disabled / sending' map to, and what form should the
  feedback take?" — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** start recording
  (`Ctrl+Space`) must produce feedback; stopping must produce feedback; if
  nothing was captured, report that. (Clarifies the original seed intent
  `/intake Provide feedback when voice input is enabled/disabled/sending
  --priority high`; also resolves A3 — the empty-capture case is explicitly
  reported and "sending" is tied to the stop transition, not a standalone
  event.) Source: operator follow-up in session
  `herdr-1791369690-73813-2605`.
- Q: "Is the audible cue acceptable, and is visual feedback primary (A2)?" —
  **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking).** Operator has not addressed the audible cue;
  proceeding with A2 — visual feedback primary, optional configurable audible
  cue (`feedbackSound`, default `true`). Source: prior intake pass. **Producer
  action:** confirm A2 (or request audible-cue default `false`) before
  implementation.
